claims.behaviour: The web-resource `widget` adds no file of its own. It depends, in this order, on `widget-atlas-deps` then `widget-local-deps`, so a page that requires `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget` gets the full structure widget: Jira and AUI parts first, the plugin's own parts after them.

The web-resource `widget-local-deps` adds no file. It depends, in this order, on `fonts`, `jquery-ui`, `jsutil`, `effector-common`, `favorites`, `widget-i18n`, `widget-bare`, `wiki-editor-theme-observer` (all of plugin `com.almworks.jira.structure`). It exists so that an embedder can take the widget without the Jira and AUI group.

The web-resource `widget-atlas-deps` adds no file. It depends, in this order, on `com.atlassian.auiplugin:ajs`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:aui-select2`, `com.atlassian.jira.jira-quick-edit-plugin:quick-form`, `com.atlassian.jira.plugins.jira-editor-plugin:customization`, `com.atlassian.jira.plugins.jira-editor-plugin:registry`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:inline-dialog`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:dialog2`, `com.atlassian.auiplugin:aui-toggle`, `jira.webresources:jquery-spin`, `jira.webresources:jira-global`, `jira.webresources:jquery-fancybox`, `jira.webresources:autocomplete`, `jira.webresources:jira-fields`, `jira.webresources:calendar`, `jira.webresources:jqlautocomplete`, `jira.webresources:key-commands`. These give the widget Jira's dialogs, selects, inline dialogs, toggles, quick create and edit forms, rich editor, fancybox image viewer, date calendar, JQL autocomplete and keyboard shortcut handling. The claims below that use those Jira parts need them on the page.

Every widget runs on exactly one kind of page: board (`structure`, the default when a page sets nothing), issue page (`issue`), project page (`project`), dashboard gadget (`gadget`, with a gadget type `local`, `remote` or `macro`) or Jira Software board tab (`greenhopper`). Setting the kind clears every other page setting. A Software board id can only be set on that tab and reads 0 otherwise; a gadget id can only be set on a gadget and reads empty otherwise. These page ids are also the per-page key of the remembered layout.

Widget options a page does not set have these defaults: height 200 (see the height modes), a minimum of 2 rows and no maximum (0) of height, fixed row height 33 px, indent per depth 32 px plus 12 px, toolbar shown, closed issues dimmed, polling every 10 s, 60 s while the user is inactive, 1 s while boosted for 6 s after a change, user counts as inactive after 300 s, uploads wait 500 ms, 250 rows kept in the row cache, at least 50 rows cached, 2 screens preloaded, at least 10 rows on a screen, 2500 ms text-wrapping scroll delay, 2000 ms to hide the column edit panel and to submit an attribute editor, no details panel, not read-only, no forced or initial view, no current structure, footer not fixed to the bottom, page not hideable.

Per page kind the options default so: gadgets, issue pages and Software board tabs have a single panel, so the secondary panel never comes to life there. Issue pages and Software board tabs force the layout `single` (a forced layout is neither read from nor written to storage). The manage-saved-columns entry is off on issue pages, gadgets and Software board tabs. Jira issue actions are disabled in remote gadgets, macro gadgets and Software board tabs.

On creation the widget builds its frame, starts the primary panel at once and starts the secondary panel only the first time it is shown. It counts as started once the current script turn has ended and the URL handling is done (immediately on gadget, issue page and Software board tab). Code waiting for a ready widget runs at that moment, or at once when it already happened; if it runs with no widget on the page, it fails with the error `no <product> widget`. With several widgets on one page the last one created is the current one and a warning is logged.

The widget's frame, from top to bottom: an optional panel header and banners, the main area, a footer. The main area holds the primary panel on the left with an optional bottom panel under it, separated by a horizontal splitter; a vertical splitter (with a cross-shaped grab point where both meet) separates them from the right-hand panel. Each forest panel has a head, a grid header, banners, a body of three grid sections (sticky left, main, sticky right) and footer banners. Accessible names, exactly: `Main widget panel`, `Secondary widget panel`, `Grid header`, `Left grid section`, `Main grid section`, `Right grid section` (each section has the tree-grid role), `Widget footer`, `Panel content status`, `Undo or redo`.

The footer holds, in this order: the info control (name `Info`, description `Show information about <product>`, button role), the board link, the secondary-panel status, the item count, the duplicates toggle, the `hit limits` and `looping` generator toggles, the progress spinner, footer warnings, background processes, the undo/redo link and the Confluence warning.

The footer's item count follows the focused panel's statistics, and has a long and a short form. 0 or fewer items: `No items shown` / `No items`. 1 item: `Showing one item` / `one item`. n items: `Showing n items` / `n items`, the number or the word `one` in bold. It updates on each statistics change, and 50 ms after the focused panel changes.

The footer's duplicates toggle is hidden when the focused panel has no duplicate items or ignores duplicates; otherwise it reads `1 item with duplicates` or `n items with duplicates`. It is a pressed/unpressed toggle that is two-way bound to the duplicates setting of the focused panel: clicking writes to the panel, a change in the panel changes the toggle, and the toggle reloads its state when focus moves to another panel.

The two generator toggles in the footer are shown only when the focused panel's count is above 0 and the page is not an issue page, gadget or Software board tab. They read `1 generator hit limits` / `n generators hit limits` and `1 generator looping` / `n generators looping`. Each is bound both ways to the matching banner of the focused panel header: on means the banner is open.
When the focused panel changes, the `hit limits` toggle reloads from the new panel but the `looping` toggle keeps its old pressed state until that banner next changes (as the original does).

A page can ask the footer to adapt to its width: the sum of the outer widths of the visible footer parts (ignoring the clearing element) is measured with the compact mode off, and compact mode turns on when that sum exceeds the footer's width. In compact mode the short forms of the item count and of undo/redo show. It is measured at once, on every window layout, and, at most once per 100 ms, when the panel's view adjustments, the error states, the undo text or the item count change.

The undo/redo link is hidden while history is shown and when there is nothing to undo. Otherwise its short form reads `Undo` or `Redo` (by whether the action is currently applied) and its long form reads `Undo <action>` or `Redo <action>`, where action is one of `Move Up`, `Move Down`, `Outdent`, `Indent`, `Drag and Drop`, `Remove`, `Paste`, `Add` (for add-from-search). When the undo record is marked fading, the link fades out over 10 s (`UNDO_FADEOUT_TIME`); the undo lifetime is 60 s. Clicking the link runs the undo-or-redo action of the panel.

Fixed limits of the UI: column width 16 to 10000 px; item editor panel width 100 to 3000 px and height 50 to 5000 px; a row render delay of 25 ms; at most 400 characters of parameters in a GET page opening (see the page opening rule); undo lifetime 60 s and fade-out 10 s.

The footer spinner is visible while the upload queue is not idle, attribute values are loading or history is loading. Its state is re-evaluated 200 ms after an upload-queue, row-data or forest loading change, so a very short activity does not show. It is hidden (its space stays) otherwise.

Footer warnings are keyed. Showing a key replaces any earlier warning of that key and puts it on top; only the most recent one shows, as an icon and a link with the given message, both with the given tooltip, and clicking either runs its action. Hiding a key removes it and reveals the next most recent one; with none left the area hides. The ordinary warning and the Confluence warning are two independent stacks with different icons.

The widget is read-only when any of these holds: the page forces read-only; the history panel is shown; the server configuration carries a `globalError` (`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`). The licence state never causes it, and the licence warning `Structure is read-only (invalid license)` never appears. Transformations are disabled while automation is on or history is shown.

Automation mode starts off. It can be switched by the toggle action (shortcut `` ` `` or `shift+`` ` ``) and is switched on when the URL fragment's `itemId` is an automation item. On issue pages, gadgets and Software board tabs it stays off whatever is asked. Clicking the 'automation on' warning, while automation is on, asks to turn it off.

After the widget configuration (`GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/widget`) has loaded, a non-null `globalError` turns on read-only. Missing `canCreate` or `canBulkChange` only sets a marker on the widget that no rule or script uses, so nothing visible changes because of it here; the controls concerned check these rights themselves.

When the user is about to leave the page, in this order: the UI state (selection, expansion, focus, scroll) is saved at once; a warning set by anyone else first wins; then, when any panel has uncommitted edits, the browser's leave prompt shows `Some of the item edits were not uploaded. If you leave this page now, those changes will be lost.`, a blank line, `Changed: <names>` (with `one new item` or `n new items` as the last name), and, when the upload queue is blocked, a blank line and a sentence saying that structure changes are waiting because a new item failed and how to fix it; then, when uploads are pending, a question panel shows and the prompt reads `We're still uploading changes to the server. If you leave this page now, some of the changes you've made may be lost.` Otherwise no prompt shows and error reporting is turned off, so requests cut off by leaving show no error.

Only one family of popups is open at a time. Showing a popup closes all others unless it is opened as a nested one; showing one that is already open does nothing. Closing the current popup (the most recent) reports whether there was one to close, so Esc can close the popup and do nothing else.

A shortcut's action goes to the focused panel, or, without one, to the panel holding the event target, or else to the widget. The browser's default handling goes on unless the action consumed the event. The default shortcut table is claimed with the action registry; a table entry marked as pass-through (the Jira `g` prefix) leaves the key to Jira.

The widget's shortcuts are off while any Jira dialog, AUI dialog, the manage-views popup, the Assets dialog or the planning task creation dialog is open: the first one opened turns them off, the last one closed turns them back on (the dialogs are counted). While a dialog that asks to ignore Jira shortcuts is among the open ones, Jira's own shortcuts are also ignored.

While an AUI dropdown is open the widget ignores Enter, the arrow keys, Space, Esc, Tab, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End and any key already handled, so they drive the dropdown. Other keys still reach the widget.

Any link, button or form in the page marked as a widget action, when clicked or submitted, runs that action on the panel that contains it (else the widget), passes the input values of its enclosing form if it names one (for a form, the form's own inputs), and cancels the browser's default.

Printing and exporting use the focused panel and send these fields: `forestSpec`, the panel's spec as JSON, for the REST API. For a structure with history shown and a chosen version, it gets `version` and loses `transforms`; for a structure with automation on and no history, it gets `title: true` and loses `transforms`. `viewSpec`, the JSON of an adjusted view (each column without a name takes it from the panel's current column), or, for an unadjusted view, `viewId`. `expand`, the expansion state in the text form. `clientFilter`, only with a user filter on. `signature`, of the forest's current version, or 0. `atl_token`, the Jira XSRF token.

The print action opens `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa` in a window named `strprint` plus the panel's settings key, so printing the same structure reuses the window. The Excel actions open `/plugins/servlet/structure/excel` in the same window with the fields above plus `xlsx` = `true` or `false`. With no focused panel nothing opens. See the page opening rule.

The UI opens a page with parameters through a hidden form to the context-relative URL. It uses GET, unless the caller fixed a method, or POST when the sum over the parameters of (name length + value length + 2), both URL-encoded, is above 400. The earlier hidden form is replaced, so only one stays on the page.
The 'extra actions' action hides the widget's extra-action controls when any of them is visible, and otherwise shows them all.

On gadgets, Software board tabs, issue pages and project pages the footer has a link `Open`, tooltip `Open <product> Board`, target `_top`, to `<context>/secure/StructureBoard.jspa?s=<JSON>[#view=<id>][&rowId=<id>]`. The JSON, URL-encoded, is the primary panel's spec with a `transforms` array first (empty when absent) and each transform's `id` and `permanent` removed. `view` is the base view of the focused panel, when it has one; `rowId` the focused row of the primary panel, joined with `#` when there is no view. It is hidden with no spec. It updates when the primary panel's spec, focused row or view changes. It does not exist on the board.

Board link examples for spec `{"structureId":7}`: view 3 and row 12 gives `?s=%7B%22transforms%22%3A%5B%5D%2C%22structureId%22%3A7%7D#view=3&rowId=12`, no view and row 12 gives `...#rowId=12`, neither gives no fragment.

The cover for 'pinned issue is missing from structure' with its two actions never shows, since the conditions it listens to do not exist; a pinned item missing from the structure gives no cover here (as the original does). The start-up hint for an empty primary panel shows nothing either.

Rows removed from the primary panel are kept in a local list while an undo record exists, and that list is dropped of the rows that have returned when the undo record goes away. Nothing shows it to the user; it has no visible effect.
Rows and attribute records in the browser are numbered from one page-wide counter that starts at 1 and only increases.

A page script can do the following to the widget: show a structure in the primary or secondary panel (a number means that structure id); focus an item or a row once when it appears; pin the view on an anchor issue and clear it; force or set a view, or set the initial one; change the layout; show a history version; enable or disable keyboard handling or error reporting; ask or clear a question in the decision panel; show the single-structure mode (issue page and Software board tab only, and a no-op elsewhere); force a new layout, optionally after clearing measured sizes; add further forest panels, which then count like any panel for focus and statistics.
Fragment form `#<positive number>`: on start-up the row of that number is focused once, and the fragment is cleared.

When the server reports the user logged out, an error message in Jira's message area, closable, with no timeout, reads `You are no longer logged in. Please log in to continue.`, with `log in` a link to `<context>/login.jsp?os_destination=<URL-encoded current page path, query and fragment, without the context path>`.

Widget option `height` takes `window` (fill the browser window), `container` (fill the nearest scrollable ancestor, or the body), `model` (fit the content), `model+selectors` (fit the content but at least the open column selector) or a number of pixels for the grid body. Any other value, or a number of 0 or less, means `model`. The grid's body height stays between minimum rows × row height (2 × 33 = 66 px by default; a negative result counts as 0) and maximum rows × row height, where 0 means no maximum.

In `window` mode the page height is the window height less everything visible around it: the project page head, Jira header, banners and messages, the board header or toolbar, the focus decoration and the footer. It applies on document ready, without animation, and at every window layout, where the change is animated for 100 ms unless the current height is out of range or a panel was just opened. It is measured again 100 ms after a window resize, 100 ms after a Jira warning or header message is removed, and when the websudo banner is closed.

In `window` mode, while the toolbar is revealed by hover in full screen, the height of the toolbar is not a number, so a window layout in that state cannot compute a height and the page height stays as it is (as the original does).

In `model` mode the page follows, recalculated on any change, the largest of: the column selector height (`model+selectors` only), the item editor height, the primary banners' height plus the smaller of (maximum height + the grid's extra editor height) and the content height, and the footer warning height. Content height is the larger of the two panels' content, plus 17 px when the primary view scrolls horizontally. It starts when the widget starts, with no animation.

A side panel's width is computed so: take the wanted width, raise it to the panel's minimum; if the main panel would then have less than its minimum (500 px), reduce the side panel by the shortage, but not below its own minimum; round. Bottom panel height works the same against the main panel's minimum height (186 px plus its banners). Example: page 1000 px, no splitter width, secondary minimum 500: wanted 700 gives 500; wanted 300 gives 500.

Panel sizes: secondary, default half of the page width, minimum 500 px; details, default 1200 px, minimum 425 px; history, default 300 px, minimum 200 px; an external panel, its own default and minimum; bottom panel, default half the free height, minimum 182 px unless the panel gives its own. When the panel cannot be fitted beside the main panel the side panel shrinks first and then the main panel, down to their minimums. A page of no width moves the side panel away.

A panel's size is remembered as a share of the page in ten-thousandths (rounded down), per panel and dimension, for each user's browser, 100 ms after it last changed. It is reread each time the panel opens. Values outside 1..9999 count as no value. In a perspective it is stored as `pageManager.<panel>.width` or `.height`, for only the side and bottom panel on show, and a perspective need not contain it. After a window resize the size is recomputed from the share, 100 ms after the last resize event.

Splitters are dragged by the left mouse button. The vertical splitter works only with a side panel on show and a page wider than 10 px, and changes its width; the horizontal one needs the bottom panel, and changes its height; the cross point changes both. Moving the splitter to the left widens the side panel; moving it up raises the bottom panel. While dragging, the page follows at once, text selection is off and the same 'resizing' state shows on all splitters. On release the new size is stored as a share. A press while a drag is in progress is ignored.

Window focus and blur on the window or document (not on elements inside) are passed on to the widget; other handlers of the page still run. In a hideable widget, every 5 s the widget checks whether it became visible or hidden, tells its parts, and on becoming visible lays itself out again.

The widget has four built-in layouts: `single`, `double` (with the secondary panel), `details` and `history`, and any number of external ones. Menu `Layout` shows `Single Grid`, `Double Grid`, `Grid + Details`, `Grid + History`; the Details entry shows only with the details panel configured, and external entries are added with their menu text, or their name, at the end. Shortcuts `ctrl+alt+1` to `4` (and numpad) pick them, on non-gadget, non-issue-page and non-Software-tab pages only.

The chosen layout is remembered per page kind in the browser (a default of `single`), and in a perspective as field `layout`. A restored `double` without a secondary spec falls back to `single`. A forced layout overrides this and is not stored.

A layout change may be refused, and then the previous value stays, also in the menu: leaving `double` needs the secondary panel to allow it (no uncommitted changes, or the user agrees); leaving `details` needs the details panel to allow it; and every change may be prevented by a listener told the current and new layouts. While a layout is being applied, a further change request is refused.

Closing details or history returns to the layout in use before them: the last of `single`, `double` or external, or at first `double` with a secondary spec and `single` without. If none is known it uses the next-layout rule: from `single` go to `double`; from `details` without a configured details panel go to `double`; from anything else go to `single`. Opening details or history from elsewhere switches to that layout.

When an external panel registers (through the browser API's panel registry): once the widget started it gets an action named after it, with its toggle text as title, and the next free shortcut from `ctrl+alt+5` up (with the numpad form). Its menu entry is added, or shown if it was already there. If it is the stored layout, it opens now. An external panel whose extension the server says is not available goes back to the previous layout, or `single`. An unknown layout hides the side panel.

Which parts count as visible per layout: the primary panel, always; the secondary panel, only in `double`; details, only in `details`; history, only in `history`; text wrapping of rows, in `single`, `double` and `details`, not `history`. For any other part an external layout decides, and the part named `gantt-resources` is visible in layout `ganttWithResources`.
Every change of layout from 3 s after creation on counts `layout.switch` in usage statistics.

On the board only, a menu section offers `Full Screen` and `Mark Manual Adjustments` as checkboxes, plus a chevron toggle for the toolbar. The display state comes from four inputs: not full screen gives `normal`; full screen with toolbar on gives `tbon`; full screen with toolbar off gives `tboff`, or `tbhov` while the mouse hover is on or a toolbar dropdown is open. Off the board the section is removed and none of this applies. The shortcut is `z`.

Going full screen collapses Jira's header (height 41 px to 0); with `tboff` the board header shrinks to 6 px and the toolbar is out of view, with `tbon` or `tbhov` it stays at 44 px. Each change animates for 75 ms and then lays out again. In `tbhov` the toolbar lies over the grid, and the grid keeps its size and position. The page starts in the remembered state without animation. The Jira header is put back on returning to `normal`.

With the toolbar off in full screen: the mouse staying 200 ms on the hover strip, or entering the toolbar, reveals it; leaving the board header for 1000 ms hides it; a click outside the board header hides it at once; while a toolbar dropdown is open it stays, and for 500 ms after the dropdown closes. Choosing a toggle in the menu or the chevron clears the hover.
Three booleans are remembered in the browser and in a perspective as fields `fullScreen`, `toolbarOff` and `showAdjustments`, written as the strings `true` and `false`. Defaults: false, false, true.
Changing `Mark Manual Adjustments` recreates the columns of all panels, so the adjustment mark shows or goes at once.

One forest panel is focused at a time, primary by default, and remembered in the browser and in a perspective as field `pageManager.focusedPanel` with the value `primary` or `secondary`. An unknown name means primary. Pressing the mouse in a panel focuses it. The focused panel is marked, and the actions, footer and toolbar follow it.

The `\` shortcut moves focus: with a bottom panel, between that and the primary; with the secondary, between both panels; with details, between details and the grid; with history or nothing beside the grid, it does nothing. The key is consumed only when the secondary panel is showing; in every other case it goes on to the browser and Jira.
When a panel gains focus and has no focused row, its first row gets focus, if there is one. Otherwise the panel reports its current focused row again, so the details and toolbar follow.

While details or history is shown and focused, the grid panel loses its focus mark. When details or history closes or loses focus, focus returns to the primary panel, and closing history also re-enters the primary panel as above.

A forest panel can be placed under the primary panel, for add-ons; it shares the same header space. It has a horizontal splitter above it, and the cross point shows only with it. Its height is stored like other sizes, and the height of the primary body is reduced by the bottom panel plus the splitter.

`alt+\` swaps the two panels' content: it is on only on the board, in `double`, with no cell being edited in either panel, and with no dropdown, column edit or add panel, dialog or inline dialog on show. Each panel takes the other's spec without transforms, the other's base view, its header and footer state and UI state (expansion, selection, focus, scroll). Then focus moves to the other panel. The fields `ph.multi.selection`, `ph.quick.transforms` and `ph.transforms` of the perspective state have their `p1` and `p2` exchanged. A swap in progress blocks another until both panels have reloaded their UI state; when the swap left the structures unchanged, that reload is triggered explicitly.

Board and project page URLs carry: `s`, the primary spec; `rs`, the secondary spec; `v`, the history version; `view`, a forced view id; `p`, a perspective id. `s` and `rs` are a plain structure id, or else URL-encoded JSON of a spec. A spec holding only a structure id is written as the number: `?s=12`. Anything else is JSON of the spec without `transforms` and `title`, and with `pinnedItem` last when set, for example `s=%7B%22structureId%22%3A12%2C%22pinnedItem%22%3A%2210001%22%7D`.

On start-up the query is read so: no `s` and no `p` with a current structure in the page's configuration means that structure. `p` installs the perspective (details with the perspective claims). `view` forces the view, `v` shows that history version. Per panel, a value of `s`/`rs` that is a non-zero number is a structure id and anything else is parsed as JSON. With a perspective, its spec fills in a missing value, and the `transforms` of the result are dropped whichever source it came from. `pinnedItem` is set to null when missing.
A value of `s` or `rs` that is neither a number nor valid JSON is not caught, so start-up stops there and the widget never reports itself started (as the original does).

The fragment of a board or project URL is `&`-joined `name=value` pairs, URL-decoded; a part without exactly one `=` is ignored. It is read once at start-up, after the query. `view=<id>` sets the initial view (it is not forced); `layout=<name>` asks for that layout; `itemId=<item identity>` focuses that item once, turning automation on first when it is a generator or effector; `rowId=<number>` focuses that row once; `effectorProcessDialog=<process id>` opens the effect process dialog. Example: `#layout=details&itemId=...` (see `generic-item-type-helper` for a link of this form).

After reading, those five names are removed from the fragment with `history.replaceState`; other pairs stay in their order: `?s=1#view=3&x=y` becomes `?s=1#x=y`, and `?s=1#view=3` becomes `?s=1#`. Without any of the five, the URL is not touched.

The fragment is also matched as slash-separated flags at load: `debug`, `betamode`, `nobetamode` (wins over `betamode`) and `devmode`, as whole segments, so `#debug` and `#x/debug/y` both match. `debug` turns on assertions and debug logging; these flags only change logging and developer controls, and they do not stay after reload unless still in the fragment. In beta mode on board or project pages, page script errors from plugin or `.jspa` code are logged as errors, others as warnings.

While the page is open the URL follows the panels: `s` from the primary spec, `rs` from the secondary spec only when the secondary panel is on show (it is removed in `single` and `history`), `v` from the chosen history version, 0 removing it. Other parameters, the fragment included, are kept. With no primary spec the URL stays. The change is applied 10 ms after the last state change. If the fragment is empty the URL gets a bare `#`, as in `?s=1#`.

The first URL write replaces the history entry, when the URL differs. Later ones write only when the query's parameters really differ, and add a history entry when a panel changed to another structure or kind of forest (or the secondary panel came or went), else they replace the entry. Failures of the history API are logged and ignored.

On browser Back or Forward, once start-up is complete and no URL write is pending, if the query differs from what the state would write, then the panels take the specs from the URL, the layout becomes `double` with `rs`, `history` with `v`, otherwise `single`, and `view` and `v` apply as at start-up. A URL with just `?` is ignored.

The window title is `<primary name> - <original page title>`; in `double` with a secondary name, or with an external panel giving its title text, `<primary> | <second> - <original>`. A missing name reads `Unknown Structure`. It is updated 10 ms after the last change, and not while a URL write is pending; a change of the structure updates it just after that write.

Gadgets, issue pages and Software board tabs ignore the URL: no query or fragment is read or written and the document title is left alone. A macro gadget reads the URL once at start-up as a board does, but does not follow state or Back and Forward.

Per panel, a user's browser remembers: expansion, focus and scroll, each per forest key (the structure id, else spec `type`, else `cql` or `sQuery`), with no key meaning not remembered; selection, per panel only, for the browser session, and never in gadgets. Scroll is not remembered on issue pages. A gadget's state is prefixed by its window name, a Software board tab's by a shared tab prefix, so these do not collide with the board. Saving waits 500 ms after the last change (the leave-page save is immediate).

In a perspective the UI state is under `<panel>.uiState` in fields `expansion`, `focus`, `scroll` and `selection`, with panel `primary` or `secondary`. While a perspective is on, changes go to the session only, per perspective. Row lists that are not arrays of numbers are reported as a perspective problem; negative numbers in them are dropped.

Saved UI state is JSON. Each object has `groupLevels` (grouping generators in the spec, plus one with a title row) and `signature` of the forest. `expansion` adds `expansionLevel` and `expanded`; `selection` adds `defaultSelected`, `hideUnselected`, `selected`; `focus` adds `focusedPath`; `scroll` adds `scrolledPath`, `rowScroll`, `viewPortScroll`. A row map (`expanded`, `selected`) is an array of `[{"rowId":n,"path":[[itemId,semantics],...]}, value]`, in forest order, for rows in the forest. A path (`focusedPath`, `scrolledPath`) is one object of the same form `{"rowId":n,"path":[...]}`, the deepest row still in the forest, or `{}`.

Restoring finds rows so: with the same non-zero signature, a row is its row id or nothing. Otherwise a row id that is persistent (positive and even) and in the forest is kept. Otherwise rows are matched by the path of item and semantics; when the forest now has more group levels than the saved path that many forest levels may be skipped, and when it has fewer that many saved levels may be skipped. For a map, every matching row is restored; for a path, the first. If nothing matches and the group levels are equal and non-zero, paths of the same length and the same levels below the groups are scored by how many saved groups occur among the current ones, in any order, and the best score wins (for a path, the first of them). For a path, shorter prefixes are tried.
Restored `expansionLevel` is shifted by the change in group levels, never below 0: saved at 2 with 1 group and restored with 3 groups gives 4.

A panel loads its state when it knows the forest spec and its version. It loads again, including the selection, when the spec or the signature changes. When a panel starts following a forest of another forest key the selection is not restored and stays empty. State is saved first when the panel stops following a forest. With no forest key nothing is stored or restored. Restore order: expansion, focus, scroll, then selection, then scroll is applied, and only then do listeners hear that the UI state was loaded.

When the server replaces temporary rows by real ones in an untransformed forest, focus, expansion and selection move to the new row ids, without a selection-changed notice; if the focused row changed, the focus notice comes in the next script turn.
When the forest changes, selected and expansion records of rows no longer in it are dropped, except when a pinned item is set, in history mode or while an undo record is in effect.

A row is expanded when the title row, when marked expanded or collapsed explicitly, or else when its depth is below the expansion level (starting at 0). Marking a row as its default clears the mark. A row on a force-expanded path cannot be collapsed. The title row can never be collapsed.

When search or filter gives root paths, every row above the matches is force-expanded and expanded, and stays so until the root paths change; a change first clears the earlier force list but leaves the rows expanded.

`Expand all` sets the level to 10000 and `collapse all` sets it to 0, or 1 with a title row. Next or previous level adds n: when n is negative the level is first cut to the deepest row's depth; a level that reaches the deepest depth becomes 10000 (level 10000, deepest depth 3, n = -1 gives 2). A level is kept between 0 and 10000 and other input is ignored. Any such call, even for the same level, clears the individual marks; only when going up to a value strictly between 0 and 10000 are expanded marks of rows the new level does not cover kept. Force-expanded rows always stay.

The expansion text form is the level and then one entry per marked row joined with dots, `+` for expanded and `-` for collapsed, in insertion order: `2.+100.-104`. With no marks it is the level alone, `0`. See `expand` of `/secure/StructurePrintable.jspa`.

Restoring a focus path marks every ancestor of it as expanded, so the focused row shows. Asking for the visible stand-in of a row inside a collapsed subtree gives its nearest visible ancestor, by cutting the path at the first row that is not expanded.

The focused row is the last of a focused path, cut to the first collapsed row, so focus is never inside a collapsed row. Each change is saved after 500 ms, reports new and old row to listeners, sets the selection anchor to the new row and picks a candidate for the case the row gets deleted.

When the focused row is no longer displayed, focus goes to: the deletion candidate if displayed; else the deepest ancestor that is still displayed; else the first row. A saved focus path that fails moves to its deepest row that still exists, and its ancestors are expanded on restore.

Focusing a row by id fails quietly when the row is unknown. It can open the ancestors first, and it can extend the selection (shift behaviour): the selection becomes the displayed rows between the anchor and the target, inclusive, and the anchor stays. When the anchor is gone, it is its nearest displayed ancestor, then the focused row, then the first row. Extending to the anchor row itself gives an empty selection.

Selection is explicit and separate from focus. It has a default (all or none) and per-row exceptions. The title row is never selected. When nothing is selected, the focused row acts as the selection, for counts and for actions, and shows as automatically selected. 'Select all' toggles between all and none by asking whether everything in the expanded forest is selected. Exceptions of rows not in the forest do not count.

Selection commands act from the focused row: select subtree adds the focused row and all its descendants to the current selection; deselect subtree removes them; select roots selects the top-most rows of the selection, or nothing when that is just the focused row. All give an explicit selection.

The normalised selection used for moving and copying holds rows whose ancestors are not selected, the title row left out; with select-all it skips unselected rows and takes each next subtree whole. The selection's order is forest order.
'Hide unselected' is restored from saved state only when something is selected in the filtered forest. It is saved with the selection.

The saved scroll has the path of the focused row if visible (else the second visible row), the row's position in the view as ten-thousandths, and the viewport's position as ten-thousandths; at the very top or bottom, or in an empty forest, the path is empty and the row position is 0. It is captured on focus by row and before leaving. Restoring places the saved row at the saved height if it is displayed, else it uses the viewport share. On issue pages it never moves. A row outside the visible range is not recorded.

A left press in a grid row focuses that row (if another) and its panel. Pressing the multi-select mark does not change the row focus. The press does nothing outside a panel. A drag from the row is tried first and wins; drag rules are with the drag-and-drop claims.
A left press on a row's expander flips that row's expansion, counts `expandClick` or `collapseClick` in statistics, and stops there: no focus change and no drag.

With a cell editor open, a left press on a row moves the editor: to the pressed cell when it is editable, otherwise the same column on the pressed row. If the move succeeded, or the press hit a link, the row is not focused, and default handling stops. With no editor open but a row that has failed uploads, pressing it opens the pressed cell if that has errors, otherwise the first cell with an error.

A plain left double-click in a cell opens the editor of that row and column, cancels a pending link click and stops other handlers. Nothing happens outside a cell. Clicks inside the editor panel, a dropdown, the multi-select mark, on the expander, or in an overflow hint outside its name are not handled here.

A plain left click on a link in a row does not navigate at once: its default is cancelled, and for an issue link Jira's handlers are kept out too. 550 ms later, unless a double-click came, and if the link is still on the page, listeners may stop it, otherwise the navigation hint is saved and a new click is sent to the link, which passes unhindered, so the browser or Jira follows it. If that click is cancelled and the link is no issue link, its `href` opens in its target (default `_self`). A modified click (ctrl, shift, alt, meta) or middle click goes through at once.
After a plain left click in a row, text selection is off and comes back 500 ms after, to keep double-clicks from selecting text.
With a cell editor open, a plain click on a link outside the editor panel is swallowed: it neither navigates nor reaches other handlers.

A click on a label link in a grid cell never navigates. With automation off it adds a filter transform to that panel: `{key:"filter", module:"com.almworks.jira.structure:filter-jql", params:{jql:<q>}}`, with q the link's `jql` parameter or else `labels = "<label text>"`. An equal one is not added twice, and an empty label does nothing. With automation on it does nothing.

When the user opens an issue from a structure, by a link under `<base>/browse/` with an issue key, or otherwise via an open-issue action, cookie `structure3.navigation.hint` is set to `<structure id>|<ms since epoch>|<ISSUE-KEY>` for 1 day, path = the context path with a trailing slash, so `/jira/` or `/` (see `ui-configurator`). Only panels showing a structure do it. Keys come from `/browse/KEY-123` with an optional query or fragment after, uppercased.
The hint can be read and cleared at once (clearing is by an expired cookie), and put back, with the 1-day life renewed, when the action turns out not to navigate.

The widget's own REST calls go one at a time through a queue. The next starts 50 ms after a new task or just after the last one ended; higher priority first, uploads (2) before downloads (1). In the debug block mode no call starts.

Queued calls default to GET, JSON, content type `application/json; charset=UTF-8`, timeout 60 s, on context-relative URLs. In a remote gadget they carry explicit `Accept: application/json, text/javascript, */*; q=0.01` and `Content-Type` headers. A task whose pre-check fails ends without a call.

A reply that is an object with only `jobId` means a server job is running: the same call repeats with that reply as body, after a wait of 1, 2, 4, 8, 15, 30, then 60 s for every further round. The wait table is replaced by the server's `restAsyncBackoff` when configured. The call's completion handlers run only at the end. Any other reply or an error resets the wait table position.

A 304 counts as success with no data. A success with status 0, no status text and no data means the connection failed, so it goes the error way. Tasks are not retried automatically unless they ask to; such a task loses 1 of priority on each retry. Errors in callbacks are logged and do not stop the queue.
The text of a failed call is, by preference, `localizedMessage`, then `message` of a JSON reply, then the raw response text.

All paths the UI uses have the `/rest/structure/1.0` or `/rest/structure/2.0` prefix of SPEC.md section 1.3, and `/rest/structure-pages/1.0` belongs to the Confluence companion app (`space/modifiable`, `error/ignore/system`, `error/retry/user`, `confluence/<id>/space/<key>/blueprints`), which is absent unless that integration is set up.

The widget counts usage locally: each action run through the widget and each explicit statistic adds 1 to a counter of that exact name. Counters live in a one-day bucket, whose timestamp is the local midnight in ms. They are written to browser storage 1 s after the last count. Nothing goes to the vendor.

On the first count after a local midnight, the old bucket is set aside and 120 s later sent with `POST /rest/structure/1.0/statistics/record`, body `{"timestamp":<ms>,"stats":{"name":count}}`, as an upload task. A bucket set aside and left over from an earlier visit is sent 120 s after page load. On success it is deleted. On failure it is sent again after 120 s, and after the third failure it is dropped with a log warning.

On creation the widget counts `widget.created`, then `widget.created.<page>`, `widget.created.<browser>` and `widget.created.<page>.<browser>`. Page is: `issue`; `gadget` and `gadget.<type>`; `pcv` and `pcv.project`; `agile`; `structure-with-details` and `structure-with-details.board` when the details panel is shown; else `board`. Browser is each that applies of `ie`, `ie7` to `ie11`, `mozilla`, `webkit`, `chrome`, `safari`, `mac`.

Browser storage rules: values are strings. A normal value is written to both session and local storage. A session-only value goes to the session store. When neither store exists, values are kept in memory for the page. Reading tries session, then local, then memory. A value missing or unreadable reads as empty; a store that throws is ignored. So a tab keeps its own value, and a new tab takes the last value written by any tab.
Loading the widget leaves Jira's global `$` and `jQuery` set to Jira's own jQuery. The widget keeps its own reference.

`ctrl+/` or `ctrl+shift+/` opens a large Jira dialog with content from `GET /secure/ViewStructureShortcuts.jspa` (`?mac=true` on a Mac). It opens only when the widget is visible. The dialog's body takes focus so that it scrolls by keyboard, and Jira's shortcuts do not fire there.

JQL editors load their field and function names and reserved words once per page by `GET /secure/StructureSearchData.jspa`, uncached; lists that cannot be parsed are empty, with a warning, and a failed load still lets the editor work without suggestions.

A JQL field gets Jira's autocomplete with a 0.65 s delay, minimum query length 0, arrow keys wrapping, no automatic first choice. A click in the field closes the list. It parses the current value at once. It also sets Jira's advanced search help link to Jira's own documentation.

Installed JQL validation sends `GET /rest/structure/2.0/query/validate` with `type=jql` and `q=<trimmed text>` 500 ms after typing stops. A reply with non-empty `errors`, or a failed call, shows the error state; other replies show the good state; an empty field shows neither and sends nothing.

The view options popup has two toggles, `Text Wrapping` and `Horizontal scrolling` (keys `v,w` and `v,h`), with pressed state that follows the current view. It takes focus on opening and returns it when it hides. Esc inside runs the opener's cancel.

Text Wrapping is disabled in layouts that do not show it (see the layout's visible parts): the click does nothing, the shortcut too, and the tooltip reads `Text wrapping is not available with this layout`.

Local URLs join the context path and the path with one `/`; a path already starting with the context stays. With no known context, `/` is used. `/browse/<key>` makes an issue URL, with no key null. A remote gadget may override the context path.
The XSRF token is read at page load from the `atlassian-token` meta element of the topmost same-origin window (else the parent).

On pages other than issue pages and Software board tabs, Jira's 'current issue' follows the focused row of the focused panel: Jira's own issue shortcuts and dialogs then act on that issue, and its id and key are empty when the row is not an issue. The page counts as an issue navigator with a selected issue (set 800 ms after start).
On those same pages Jira's own document shortcuts `e`, `a` and `l` are removed, so the widget's take over.

Except on issue pages, a Jira dialog that would reload the page after its operation instead closes and tells the widget that items may have changed, and the page stays. A reload asked with arguments still goes through Jira's normal code.
On the issue page Jira's 'issue refreshed' event tells the widget that items may have changed.

Jira dialogs opening and closing are told to the widget. 100 ms after a Jira workflow transition dialog hides, its leftover dialog and triggers are destroyed. A dialog opened by an issue action link always asks for `inline=true` content. The labels dialog copes with a missing label list by using an empty set.
A Jira assignee picker with no fixed query forgets its last query when its pagination resets, so it asks the server again.
In Firefox, Jira's assign-to-me element loses its usual id at widget start, so Jira's own handling of it stays out of the way of the widget's.

Attachment thumbnails open Jira's fancybox as an image gallery that cycles, closes on an image click, with 300 ms fades and 150 ms between images. While it is open the widget's and Jira's shortcuts and Jira's keyboard scrolling are off; closing restores them. If fancybox is missing, nothing happens.

Jira single selects made by the widget return to the previous value on invalid input and do not remove it on unselect. A value not in the list is logged, except `None`, and shows `None`. Enter with its suggestions closed submits the surrounding form. An unset value reads `0` unless the caller sets another empty value. In a remote gadget none is created; the plain field stays, and asking to expand it focuses it. A select shows groups and items from a server search reply of `groups` with `label`, `footer`, `items` (`value`, `label`, `title`, `icon`, `html`). Groups with no items are left out, and group entries with only disabled items do not show.

Date pickers use Jira's calendar: years 1900 to 2099, week numbers shown (not ISO numbering), 24-hour clock unused, first day from the configuration or Monday. Down opens it, Esc closes it; a button opens it and focuses the input. A click on a date fills the input, fires the change and closes it. Typing fires the change, except for arrow keys while it is open. It counts as a popup in the popup coordination, as a nested one.

A dynamic Jira form placed in the widget has submit disabled and gets Jira's dialog-ready event to wire its fields. Waiting for the rich editor ends when the editor is initialised or found to be in text mode, or at once if it is there. A popup can be told not to close on clicks inside it.
In a text field inside an AUI dropdown the keys left, right, home, end and backspace stay in the field. Enter on a dropdown option returns focus to the trigger that opened it.

An isolated AUI inline dialog does not become the 'current' one, so it does not close Jira's own. A wheel event's 'no scrolling' mark is readable on wrapped events, which stops grid scrolling from popups.

Creating an issue via a dialog opens Jira's quick-create form with title `Create Issue & Add to Structure`, for the given project and issue type, the type being set again when the form is ready. Given values of a previous form are filled in, with its error messages applied. With the widget available, the project list is limited to the `GET /rest/structure/1.0/config/projects` set, and when some project was filtered out the project field gets the note `Only projects enabled for <product> are offered.`

The dialog adds, beside its submit buttons, `Switch to Panel` (tooltip `Create issue using inline editors in the <product> widget`, key `alt+enter`) and link `Don't Add to Structure` (tooltip `Don't add issue to the structure, just create it.`). The first closes the dialog and continues in the widget's inline editor with the form's values and the last validation errors. The second removes the structure handling, restores Jira's own title, or else `Create Issue`, and leaves a normal Jira create dialog.

Form values carried over: every field if switching, else only the active fields; repeated names become arrays; active `project`, `timetracking`, `issuelinks`, `attachment` and `worklogged` fields without a form element are sent empty. Temporary attachments stay attached when carried to a new form.

Submitting tells the widget the new issue id and whether the 'create another' mode is on; changing project or issue type tells the widget, too. Cancel and Esc tell it to cancel. In clone mode the warning `The option to copy categories has been turned off.` shows on the form.
If the Jira dialog cannot be opened, a warning is logged, the inline editor takes over with the same values, and the dialog is not tried again on this page.

On the board, Jira's header `Create` button gets a `+` sign before its text. With the widget's focus in a panel and details not focused, a simple click creates a sibling below in the dialog, and Jira's own handler does not run if the widget took it. Otherwise Jira opens its own dialog.

Form values for actions and parameters: a named input gives its value; unchecked boxes and radios add nothing, though their name exists, with `[]`; several with one name form an array. Applying back checks a box or radio when its value equals or is in the map value. Two maps are equal with the same keys and same values, a single string equalling a one-element array.

A toggle button shows its state as pressed, turns it into an on/off on click (unless disabled), loses focus after a click, and appears unpressed while disabled. An action can also cycle a value through a fixed list of states, wrapping at the end.
Two specs are the same base when they have an equal `structureId`, equal `sQuery.type`, or equal `type`.
A horizontal panel that opens or closes with animation fades for 500 ms with its height growing or shrinking, and the page layout then runs again; without animation it lays out at once.
A value bound to an AUI single select writes `change` only when the value differs, and reads a one-element value as a string.

When the rows on show change, the grid keeps the rendered rows of a longest common subsequence of the old and new list of row ids; ties may go either way. Equal start and end parts of the lists are matched first.
The team popup of the CFD chart shows the team name as heading and three properties in this order: `Trending Date`, `Remaining Stories`, `Predicted Stories`, with the values given by the chart.
Stored row ids that are zero or not whole numbers are dropped with a warning when focus, expansion or selection are restored, and do not stop the rest from loading.
In a remote gadget there is no clipboard: cut, copy and paste have nothing to work with and nothing is ever marked as cut.
While a perspective is active, a change of the kind of page is written into it, so that the perspective records the page it belongs to.
